- Bleached/whitish-cream stem tissue on middle and bottom stems
- Dense black specks/dots scattered across the stem surface
- Possible fluffy white material on middle stem
- Top stem has reddish-brown coloration

Top candidates: **White_Mold** (bleached stems, black sclerotia, fluffy white growth) and **Charcoal_Rot** (microsclerotia giving charcoal-sprinkled appearance on bleached stems).

Let me check reference images one at a time.

This Charcoal Rot reference shows gray-tan stem without the dense black specks. Let me check the other stem image.

Excellent match! This Charcoal Rot reference shows multiple stems with dense black specks (microsclerotia) on bleached stems - very similar to the test image. Let me check more classes for thoroughness.
Anthracnose shows reddish-brown stems, not matching the bleached stems with scattered black specks. Let me check Rhizoctonia (stem disease) and White_Mold second image.
Rhizoctonia doesn't match - it shows reddish-brown lesions at soil line. Let me check 3 more distinct classes.

I've now viewed 8 reference images across 8 classes. Summary:

- **Charcoal_Rot** (Soybean_Dise_49): Strong match - multiple bleached stems with dense fine black microsclerotia scattered uniformly, same presentation as test image
- **White_Mold**: Shows large discrete sclerotia, not fine scattered specks
- **Anthracnose**: Reddish-brown stems, not bleached
- **Rhizoctonia**: Reddish-brown sunken lesion at soil line, not matching
- **Phytophthora**: Dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration
- **Fusarium**: Greenish-white stems without the specks
- **Others**: No match

The test image shows bleached/whitish stems with dense fine black specks (microsclerotia) scattered uniformly across the surface - the hallmark of Charcoal Rot. The match to the Charcoal_Rot reference (Soybean_Dise_49) is very strong.
